_about: Cost inputs for src/cost_model.py (owner: Youcef). Prices in USD unless the key says NGN. Each value has a source or is marked as an assumption with the range tested in the sensitivity analysis. The simulation itself reads only generator_l_per_kwh.

currency.source: CBN NFEM official rate, mid-October 2026: N1,331-1,333/USD (techeconomy.ng and withinnigeria.com daily reports, 8-19 Oct 2026). Parallel market ~N1,360-1,380.

sources.pv: PVPRO, Solar equipment prices Lagos, 20 Sep 2026: 590 W mono panels N140,000-145,000 (~N240/W = $0.18/W at N1,332/USD); +10% transport to Maiduguri -> $0.20/W. Mounting: assumption.
sources.battery: BloombergNEF battery price survey, Dec 2025: LFP packs $81/kWh on average, stationary storage $70/kWh (large volumes). Small 25.6 V home modules with BMS and casing cost more: Lagos retail EasyWay 2.4 kWh 24 V LiFePO4 N855,500 = $268/kWh (PVPRO, Sep 2026). Base $180/kWh = operator buying in bulk (assumption); range $120-268 tested.
sources.charge_controller: Assumption: 24 V, 20 A MPPT charge controller at distributor price.
sources.meter_comms: Assumption: pay-per-kWh unit (energy meter, GSM modem, circuit relay). Needed by both kits, so it does not favour SABIL.
sources.sabil_controller_extra: Assumption: what the SABIL controller adds to a standard pay-per-kWh unit: two temperature sensors, a second relay to separate essential circuits, a larger microcontroller, assembly. Firmware has no per-unit cost.
sources.wiring_install_acquisition: Assumptions for Maiduguri (security and transport premium included); range tested through the capital cost.

lifetimes_years.battery: from the simulation: years until the battery holds 80% of its capacity (results/summary_*.json)
lifetimes_years.source: PV module warranties are 20-25 years; 10 years for power electronics is a common planning value (assumption).

opex.source: Assumptions: one agent visit a year and remote monitoring over GSM; theft and damage provision of 2% of the kit's value a year.

revenue_losses.source: Assumptions: mobile-money and agent fees ~2% of payments; 10% of billed energy never paid (range 5-20% tested). Pay-per-kWh limits the loss: when credit runs out only the essential circuits stay on.

finance.source: Assumption: real cost of capital of an off-grid solar company in Nigeria in USD terms; 8% (concessional finance, e.g. backed by DARES) to 18% tested.

subsidy.source: World Bank DARES Project Appraisal Document (2023): US$230 million of IDA grants for stand-alone solar for basic electrification, for 2.75 million quality-certified solar home systems -> ~$84 per system on average (our division; the real grant depends on the system tier and location). Only households in the National Social Register are eligible for the end-user price reduction.

sources.petrol: NNPC retail prices by state, 9 Oct 2026 (Legit.ng): Borno N1,430/L. NBS PMS Price Watch, March 2026: Borno N1,375/L.
sources.diesel: NBS, March 2026: average retail diesel (AGO) price N1,648/L (Businesspost.ng).
sources.small_generator: A2EI field measurements (Herzog, Schaale and Chacon, SKGS project update, 2022): small generators in Nigerian homes and shops run at ~22% of their rated load and use ~2 L of fuel per kWh.

generator_l_per_kwh_source: Used by the simulation for 'diesel avoided': a generator at a good load factor (~0.5 L/kWh). Deliberately conservative: small household generators use ~2 L/kWh (A2EI), so real fuel avoided is likely up to 4x higher.

income.sources: National Minimum Wage Act 2024: N70,000/month. HumAngle, 'The light is back on in Nigeria's Maiduguri, but residents can't afford electricity': a civil servant earning ~N50,000/month.
